content.value_statement: Boolean mode props make React components difficult to extend and understand. Apply composition guidelines to build explicit variants, shared context contracts, and reusable component parts.
actual_capabilities: Guide replacement of boolean mode props with explicit component variants.
Show compound component structures that share state through context.
Define context contracts with state, actions, and meta for interchangeable providers.
Explain how provider boundaries enable sibling components to share state and actions.
Distinguish static children composition from render props that pass data.
Provide React 19 guidance for ref as a prop and reading context with use.
limitations: Provides documentation and examples, not an executable refactoring engine or test suite.
Examples use application-specific hooks and UI components that require project implementation.
React 19 API recommendations do not apply to React 18 or earlier.
Does not verify accessibility, runtime performance, or behavioral equivalence after refactoring.

use_cases.title: Simplify Complex Component Modes
use_cases.description: Replace branching message composer modes with explicit variants that reuse shared component parts.

use_cases.title: Design Flexible Library APIs
use_cases.description: Plan compound components and provider contracts so consumers can compose layouts without adding more configuration props.

use_cases.title: Review Shared State Boundaries
use_cases.description: Assess whether previews, forms, and dialog actions share state through the right provider instead of effects or mutable refs.

prompt_templates.title: Understand a Composition Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component] and explain which boolean mode props increase complexity. Suggest explicit variants and identify the parts they could share.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: identify a focused refactoring opportunity.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Component into Parts
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [component] into compound components with children composition. Preserve existing behavior and show how each current variant composes the shared parts.

prompt_templates.title: Share State Across a Dialog
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a provider for [dialog] with state, actions, and meta. Let its form, sibling preview, and submit action share context without effect synchronization.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: define state ownership across visual boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design Interchangeable Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component family] and its React version. Design a common context contract for local and synced providers, explicit variants, and a behavior verification plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate multiple state implementations and compatibility constraints.

output_examples.input: Review a message composer with thread, editing, and forwarding mode flags.
output: Recommendation: introduce explicit ThreadComposer, EditMessageComposer, and ForwardMessageComposer variants.
Shared parts: frame, input, footer, formatting controls, and reusable actions.
Each variant selects its provider and visible actions without combining independent mode flags.

output_examples.input: A forwarding dialog has a message input, sibling preview, and separate submit button that need the same state.
output: Place one forwarding provider around the input, preview, and dialog actions.
Expose the message through state, submission through actions, and the input reference through meta.
Keep visual layout independent from state ownership so the preview and submit button can remain outside the composer frame.

output_examples.input: Should a reusable list replace its data-aware renderItem callback with children?
output_examples.output: Keep the renderItem callback when the list supplies item data and an index. Prefer children for static layout that requires no callback data.

best_practices: Check the project React version before applying React 19 API guidance.
Define a stable state, actions, and meta contract before introducing interchangeable providers.
Preserve existing behavior and verify each explicit variant after refactoring.
anti_patterns: Adding independent boolean mode props to represent mutually exclusive component variants.
Synchronizing duplicate component state through effects instead of sharing a provider.
Using render callbacks for static layout that children can express directly.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides React composition guidelines with incorrect and correct examples for component structure, context contracts, state ownership, and explicit variants.

faq.question: Does it include an executable refactoring tool?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for an AI assistant to apply within your project, not a standalone transformer or validation tool.

faq.question: Can I use it with React 18?
faq.answer: The composition and provider principles apply, but skip the React 19 API guidance and retain APIs compatible with your project.

faq.question: Are render props always discouraged?
faq.answer: No. Keep render props when a parent supplies data or state to the callback. Prefer children for static composition.

faq.question: Must shared controls sit inside the component frame?
faq.answer: No. Controls can remain outside the visual frame when they share the provider that exposes the required state and actions.

faq.question: Does the guidance require a particular state library?
faq.answer: No. It separates the context interface from provider implementation so the same UI can consume local or globally managed state.
